title: Flux window operational notes and release index
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact operational index for the April flux-window release. It combines the lightweight preflight checklist, an hourly watch-calendar for the day-of, a smoke-test bundle, and a draft copy of user-facing release notes. It is intentionally terse — use it during the launch shift as the single source of truth for actions and ownership.

Scope of this release (summary):
- Target services: api-router, model-routing, serving-runtime v2.4.1, console-dashboard minor routing tweak
- Primary goals: reduce tail-latency for 512+ token requests, add early-fallback to quantized variant when memory pressure spikes, observational feature flag for kv-cache TTL tuning
- Risk profile: medium (new kernel selector heuristics in runtime). Potential user impact limited to latency degradation; fallback paths exist.

Preflight checklist (do not mark complete until all green):
- [ ] Feature flags staged in staging and can be toggled remotely (flag keys: runtime.kernel-selector-ex, routing.fallback-quantized)
- [x] Canary build artifact created: platform-serving:v2.4.1-rc3 (build 20260406-17)
- [ ] Smoke cluster uploaded and validated with synthetic traces (replica latency < 30ms p50)
- [ ] Load-gen script updated for 512/1024 token profile (script: infra/tests/loadgen/longseq.sh)
- [ ] Rollback image placeholder registered (platform-serving:v2.4.0-stable)
- [ ] Observability dashboards pinned and alert thresholds reviewed (see linked artifacts)
- [ ] SLA owners notified and on-call rota confirmed for release day

Hour-by-hour watch-calendar (release day: 2026-04-14, UTC):
- T-3h (08:00 UTC): Release lead (Maya) - final preflight, kick Slack #release-watch, ensure runbook visible
- T-2h (09:00 UTC): Infra (Omar) - warm workers, confirm autoscaler policies behave under synthetic load
- T-1h (10:00 UTC): SRE (Linnea) - baseline telemetry snapshot captured, open grafana window: latency, error-rate, memory pressure
- T-0 (11:00 UTC): Deployment start - traffic ramp plan begins, ops watermark set to 10% initial traffic
- T+30m (11:30 UTC): Observability check - p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, 5XX counts, KV cache miss rate
- T+60m (12:00 UTC): Traffic ramp to 50% if metrics stable for last 15m
- T+120m (13:00 UTC): Full ramp decision; if degradation detected, engage rollback or binary fallback plan
- T+240m (15:00 UTC): Post-rollout retro notes captured, telemetry snapshot archived

Watchlist signals (triggers to pause/rollback):
- sustained p99 latency > baseline + 200ms for 15m
- sustained 5XX rate > 0.25% for 10m
- memory pressure > 85% on serving nodes for 5 consecutive minutes
- KV cache miss spike > 2x baseline and correlated latency increase

Rollback decision matrix (quick guide):
- minor metric blip (single metric spike < 15m): pause ramp, toggle feature flags to safe defaults, investigate
- significant multi-metric regression (latency + errors + memory): immediate rollback to v2.4.0-stable and open incident bridge
- partial region regression: shift traffic away from region, reduce capacity target, begin partial rollback for region only

Immediate actions for rapid mitigation (cheat-sheet):
- flip runtime.kernel-selector-ex -> off (falls back to legacy selector)
- enable routing.fallback-quantized -> on (routes heavy queries to quantized variant with higher CPU cost but lower memory)
- scale up dedicated serving pool by +20% (if Dedicated tenant) or add burst nodes via autoscaler policy

Smoke test bundle (run in order, results must be logged to the release ticket):
1) Health endpoints: /health, /ready - expect 200 and <100ms
2) Short-gen test (24 tokens): ensures basic output correctness and post-processing
3) Long-gen test (600 tokens): measure p50/p95 token latency and final output integrity
4) KV cache sanity: repeated prefix requests should hit cache (observed cache-hit ratio > 0.6)
5) Fallback exercise: simulate memory pressure with a synthetic worker and confirm quantized fallback triggers and responses are consistent

Telemetry and sampling notes:
- High-resolution sampling for first 90m post deploy, then relax to 1-minute rollup at T+120m
- Tag telemetry with release_id: "flux-2026-04" and rollout_lane: "gradual-window"
- Ensure traces for long-gen requests capture kernel selection path and memory usage per token (trace spans: kernel.select -> exec.batch -> kv.cache)

Draft release notes (user-facing, edit for tone/design):
- headline: Improved long-request latency and smarter fallback for memory-constrained workloads
- highlights:
  • Reduced tail latency for >512 token requests by introducing a revised kernel selection heuristic
  • Added automatic quantized fallback when node memory pressure is high to keep requests flowing
  • Small routing update to reduce cross-region proxying for Dedicated tenants
- caveats: Some experimental kernel heuristics are behind a feature flag and will be rolled out gradually. If you see unexpected latency, please contact support or use the managed dashboard to opt out.

Open questions / follow-ups (post-launch backlog):
- Add per-model cost telemetry to quantify unit-economics of quantized fallback
- Bake-in an automated canary that exercises memory-pressure fallback (ticket: ENGREL-1267)
- Decide default TTL for kv-cache by model family (proposal due end of Q2)

Notes / references / quick links:
- Release ticket: ENGREL-1245
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/981
- Console dashboard: panels -> Release / Flux window / kernel selector traces
- Slack threads: #release-watch, #sre-observability

Post-mortem stub template (fill after release):
- Summary: one-paragraph chronology
- Timeline: minute-by-minute highlights for first 4 hours
- Root cause: notes from traces and heap dumps
- Action items: owners and ETA (small PRs or infra config changes)

Quick reminders for the release lead:
- Keep the #release-watch channel focused; drive one call-to-action at a time
- If pausing the rollout, explicitly state: "rolling pause at X% — investigating" and confirm when safe to continue
- Archive a telemetry snapshot at T+0, T+60m, T+240m and attach to ENGREL-1245

Appendix (scratch):
- local commands: kubectl rollout status deploy/platform-serving -n prod --watch
- logs: krep tail --service platform-serving --since 10m | grep "kernel-selector"
